title: Ledger Coding Reference — Returned Payments, Chargebacks and the Check and ACH Restriction
content:
**Payment reversal.** When a check or ACH payment on a Patient Financial Account is returned unpaid, or a card payment is charged back, the payment entry is reversed in full, restoring the balance of the charge it had been applied to. A reversed payment is reversed once only; the ledger shows whether a reversal already exists against that payment entry.

**Returned-payment fee.** A returned check or ACH payment also posts the tier's returned-payment fee as a charge with the line category returned payment fee. No fee is posted when that amount is 0.00, and no fee is posted for a card chargeback.

| What came back | Payment reversed in full | Returned-payment fee charge posted |
|---|---|---|
| check returned unpaid | yes | yes, when the tier's fee is above 0.00 |
| ACH debit returned unpaid | yes | yes, when the tier's fee is above 0.00 |
| card payment charged back | yes | no |

**Restriction on check and ACH.** Once the account's count of returned payments — reversals of check or ACH payments dated inside the look-back — reaches the tier's number of returned payments before restriction, the account accepts only card, HSA/FSA card or cash until the look-back no longer contains that many returned payments. The look-back and the restriction both run the tier's returned-payment look-back, in calendar months.

**Hypothetical sequence.** On a class with a restriction count of 2, a 12-month look-back and a 30.00 fee: a returned check in March reverses that payment and posts a 30.00 fee; a returned ACH debit in July reverses that payment, posts another 30.00 fee and brings the count to 2, so from then on only card, HSA/FSA card or cash is accepted, until the March return drops out of the 12-month look-back and the count falls below 2.
